sovereign_question: Given an exact software source tree and available repository history, what structural, temporal, semantic and cross-layer conditions are defensibly observable, how should they be evidenced, and which bounded engineering concerns should be surfaced without minting unsupported business facts?
users_and_jobs: Software engineers inspect concrete code and dependency concerns.
Engineering leaders inspect codebase-level risk, change and ownership signals.
Architects examine module, relation, layering and evolution evidence.
Tool builders consume deterministic fact, signal, finding and snapshot outputs.
owned_meanings: Observed software file, function, class, import and repository-change facts admitted from a bounded source cut.
Application-local identities for files, commits, modules, relations, signals, findings and snapshots.
Application-local definitions of codebase structural, temporal, semantic and cross-layer findings.
Application-local evidence linking a finding to admitted source observations and method outputs.
owned_artifacts: Normalized source and Git fact set
Dependency, co-change, semantic, clone and multilayer relation graph
Per-file, per-module and global signal field
Finding set with evidence and stable identity
Analysis snapshot, diff and history record
CLI, API, server-state and rendered-report projection

source_contracts.meaning: A bounded filesystem source tree containing software artifacts and explicit discovery/exclusion policy.
source_contracts.admission_or_refusal: Admit only readable, classified files inside the selected root and policy; refuse, skip or evidence unsupported, excluded, oversized, binary or unreadable inputs.

source_contracts.meaning: An optional exact Git repository history used for commit, author, rename, file-change and co-change observations.
source_contracts.admission_or_refusal: Admit deterministic bounded history with explicit partial-history posture; absence or extraction failure must degrade visibly rather than fabricate temporal evidence.

data_shape_contracts.meaning: Source bytes, decoded text and filesystem metadata tied to an exact path and acquisition occurrence.
data_shape_contracts.admission_or_refusal: Decode under explicit fallback policy and retain skips/errors; never silently reinterpret unsupported binary content as source text.

data_shape_contracts.meaning: Language-normalized file, function, class, import, identifier and call observations with parser/fallback provenance.
data_shape_contracts.admission_or_refusal: Parser and regex-fallback results remain distinguishable; unsupported language or malformed syntax must be visible in evidence.

data_shape_contracts.meaning: Ordered commit and file-change observations including rename, deletion, author and bounded history context.
data_shape_contracts.admission_or_refusal: History must be deterministic for the selected revision/cut and expose shallow, truncated or absent history.

data_shape_contracts.meaning: Nodes and typed weighted relations for imports, co-change, similarity, clones, authorship and derived multilayer analysis.
data_shape_contracts.admission_or_refusal: Unknown or unresolved endpoints remain explicit; derived relation layers never replace their source observations.

data_shape_contracts.meaning: Typed signals, findings, provenance, snapshots and lifecycle records emitted from admitted observations and bounded methods.
data_shape_contracts.admission_or_refusal: A finding without required observations, method identity or evidence must be refused or marked unavailable, never inferred from display state.

analytical_capabilities.scope: Dependency, module, layer, cycle, reachability, centrality, community and architecture analysis over software artifacts.
Commit, churn, change-trajectory, author, rename, co-change and historical finding analysis over bounded Git observations.
Entropy, divergence, compression, concentration and related quantitative method kernels reusable only after exact semantic qualification.
Graph, hypergraph, spectral and tensor methods whose generic algorithms may be reusable but whose current application bindings are codebase-specific.
Application-specific fusion, thresholds, pattern detection and evidence assembly for software-engineering concerns.

operated_lifecycles: Discover and admit a bounded source tree.
Extract or readmit deterministic source and repository facts.
Construct typed relations and analytical observations.
Compute bounded method outputs and application signals.
Evaluate findings with evidence, refusals and degradation posture.
Persist snapshots and compare change over time.
Publish CLI, API, server and report projections without creating new source truth.
negative_charter: Does not own the universal enterprise product ontology or any retained horizontal product merely because research files share the repository.
Does not own general ERP, CRM, warehouse, lakehouse, event-stream, industrial, clinical, geospatial, document or scientific source acquisition.
Does not define universal business entities, metrics, policies, decisions, workflows, plans or industry vocabulary.
Does not constitute a general data integration, transformation, catalog, governance, quality, semantic-layer, BI, ML, optimization or planning platform.
Does not turn a Python module into a qualified semantic library without exact contract, build, execution and appraisal receipts.
Does not treat a dashboard, report or API projection as authority to mint facts, decisions or effects.
Does not claim provider portability, production SLOs, residency, cost, vertical acceptance, build readiness or ratification.
Does not make optional AI or agent behavior a prerequisite for deterministic acquisition, analysis, evidence or refusal semantics.
Does not silently broaden codebase-specific findings into universal analytical meanings.
Does not allow the research corpus to import runtime implementation details as semantic authority.

required_gates: Bind an exact abstract contract edition to each reusable implementation claim.
Record source, artifact, dependency, toolchain and configuration identity.
Rebuild reproducibly and retain provenance/SBOM evidence.
Execute exact-scope conformance, refusal, resource and failure tests.
Obtain independent appraisal and, where portability is claimed, a second independently controlled implementation.
Bind an exact physical target occurrence and execute unrelated vertical acceptance before build-ready or ratification claims.

evolution_and_exit.compatibility_facade: The existing shannon_insight import package and public API remain the application compatibility facade.
evolution_and_exit.module_split_policy: A module may move into a reusable package only after its semantic contract is separated from codebase-specific meanings and qualified independently.
evolution_and_exit.provider_substitution_policy: Provider or parser substitution requires exact capability, loss, refusal and evidence comparison; similar names or output shapes are insufficient.
evolution_and_exit.deprecation_policy: Deprecated application APIs remain explicit compatibility seams with migration evidence; they never become alternate semantic owners.
